code:
qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.x(0)   # Pauli-X: bit-flip, |0> <-> |1>
qc.y(0)   # Pauli-Y: bit-flip + phase-flip
qc.z(0)   # Pauli-Z: phase-flip, |1> sign flips
qc.h(0)   # Hadamard: equal superposition
qc.s(0)   # S gate: quarter-turn phase
qc.t(0)   # T gate: eighth-turn phase
caption: X, Y, Z are fixed, self-inverse Pauli gates. H is the workhorse that starts almost every interesting algorithm.

eyebrow: The rotation gates: RX, RY, RZ
code:
import math
qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.rx(math.pi / 2, 0)   # rotate around X by pi/2
qc.ry(math.pi / 2, 0)   # rotate around Y by pi/2
qc.rz(math.pi / 2, 0)   # rotate around Z by pi/2
caption: An explicit, adjustable angle — exactly what Chapter 6's variational algorithms tune with an optimizer.

code:
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector

qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.h(0)

sv = Statevector(qc)
print(sv)   # [0.7071068+0j, 0.7071068+0j]
caption: No sampling noise at all — the exact mathematical amplitude for every basis state.
